cards.title: Bluetooth is a short-range radio link between two devices
cards.text: Bluetooth is a short-range radio link: two devices, like a phone and an earbud, send each other data through the air as radio waves.
cards.hook: So how do two devices find each other?

notes: A phone sends radio waves straight to an earbud

cards.title: First, the two devices introduce themselves and swap keys
cards.text: To meet, one device announces itself, saying "I'm here", and the other spots it. Then they swap secret codes, called keys. The keys scramble what they send later, and let the two reconnect on their own next time.
cards.hook: Once they're connected, they have one more problem to deal with.

cards.title: Wi-Fi shares the band, so Bluetooth hops, up to 1,600 times a second
cards.text: Wi-Fi sits on the same band of airwaves as Bluetooth, so the two could collide. To avoid that, Bluetooth hops. It cuts its airwaves into dozens of narrow channels, like the stations on a radio dial, and one Wi-Fi network can cover about a quarter of that dial. So the devices never stay on one channel. Streaming music, they hop as often as 1,600 times a second. Each hop carries a tiny piece of music. If a hop lands on Wi-Fi, only that piece is lost, and it's sent again. If the resend is late, the music skips for a split second.
cards.hook: But how do the two devices know which channel to hop to next?

notes: A radio dial with a Wi-Fi block over a quarter of it
One pink channel hops along the dial
A piece lost to Wi-Fi is sent again; a late one skips

cards.title: One device sets the order of channels and the other follows it
cards.text: One of the two sets the timing and the order of channels, and the other follows it, hop for hop. That way they always land on the same channel at the same instant.
cards.hook: So what kinds of Bluetooth are there?

notes: The other follows on the same channel

cards.title: Bluetooth comes in two flavors: one streams, one sends bursts
cards.text: Bluetooth comes in two flavors. Classic streams without a break, for headphones and speakers. Low Energy sends small bursts and sleeps in between, for fitness trackers and smart tags.
cards.takeaway: Bluetooth is a short-range radio link: two devices introduce themselves once, then hop between channels together to stay clear of Wi-Fi.

notes: Low Energy sends bursts and sleeps

cards.note: Devices also use profiles, agreed sets of rules for one job, like streaming audio or a keyboard. That is how a phone knows how to talk to a speaker with no special setup.
